rounds.text: Shankara Buildpro Ltd demonstrates exceptional capital efficiency, evidenced by a stellar return on capital employed of 38.56% against a sector benchmark of just 8.26% [E10], alongside a high return on equity of 25.52% [E9]. Growth metrics are equally compelling, with compounded sales growth reaching 30% and compounded profit growth surging by 66% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. This top-line and bottom-line expansion is reinforced by robust cash generation, delivering Rs 89 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 81 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E21, E22], while maintaining a conservatively financed balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of only 0.11x [E24]. Furthermore, the business benefits from a supportive macroeconomic backdrop, as the Consumer Services sector is firmly in a tailwind with a score of +0.84, significantly outperforming the sector median sales growth of 12.0% and profit growth of 17.4% [E49, E52, E53]. Conceded: [E31], [E32], [E33].

The current market price of ₹1,212 leaves zero margin of safety at -1.0%, sitting virtually at its discounted cash flow intrinsic value of ₹1,200 [E31, E32]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price already demands a 10.1% earnings growth rate, surpassing the base case assumption of 10.0% [E33]. Institutional money flow signals negative pressure with a net holding change of -0.59 percentage points, driven by foreign institutions reducing their stake from 10.97% to 9.27% [E28, E30]. Operating margins are fragile and display an inconsistent trend over the last three quarters and the past two years, remaining flat at 4% in March 2026 compared to the previous year [E17, E18, E19]. Additionally, the stock exhibits high annualised volatility of 61.6% alongside rising borrowings, which climbed to ₹61 Cr from ₹57 Cr [E25, E39]. Conceded: the company boasts an impressive ROCE of 38.56% and strong trailing sales growth of 30% [E10, E14].

Conceded: the DCF intrinsic value sits at ₹1,200 against a market price of ₹1,212 with a -1.0% margin of safety, and the reverse DCF implies 10.1% earnings growth against a 10.0% base case [E31, E32, E33]. However, those static models completely miss the operational reality of a business generating 30% compounded trailing sales growth and 66% compounded profit growth, crushing the sector median sales growth of 12.0% and profit growth of 17.4% [E14, E15, E52, E53]. Conceded: foreign institutions trimmed their stake from 10.97% to 9.27% [E28]. Yet domestic institutions increased their holding from 12.13% to 13.24%, demonstrating robust local conviction [E29]. While the bear points to rising borrowings of ₹61 Cr, this debt level translates to a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.11x alongside ₹81 Cr in free cash flow [E22, E24, E25]. Furthermore, the rules-based screen scores the business at an 86 out of 100 with a BUY rating, backed by an elite ROCE of 38.56% that dwarfs the sector benchmark of 8.26% [E10, E43].

Conceded: trailing sales growth reached 30% and profit growth reached 66% [E14, E15]. However, that historic growth has already pushed the share price to a point where a discounted cash floor model establishes intrinsic value at ₹1,200 against a higher market price of ₹1,212, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -1.0% [E31, E32]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF reveals that the current price demands a 10.1% earnings growth rate, surpassing the base case expectation of 10.0% [E33]. Conceded: domestic institutions lifted their stake to 13.24% [E29]. Nevertheless, institutional money flow overall remains in negative territory with a holding change of -0.59 percentage points, driven by foreign institutions cutting their exposure from 10.97% to 9.27% [E28, E30]. While debt-to-equity is low at 0.11x, total borrowings climbed to ₹61 Cr and operating margins remain inconsistent across both yearly and quarterly periods, accompanied by moderate cash conversion of 0.70x [E18, E19, E20, E24, E25]. Finally, the annualised volatility of 61.6% alongside a price sitting below its 200-day moving average demonstrates significant underlying downside pressure that contradicts the bull's growth narrative [E36, E39].
